newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia starts fixed-coupon bond trading on Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: Russia starts fixed-coupon bond trading on Feb 24.

text.p: Russia will start trading fixed-rate OFZ interest-bearing government bonds on February 24 on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX), a senior Central Bank official said on Thursday.
The Finance Ministry issued the three-year paper, paying fixed interest of 20 percent a year, on June 6, 1996, First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko told Reuters.
The Finance Ministry has issued 3.8 trillion roubles worth of such paper in 12 tranches, he said.

Marina Chekurova, deputy head of the Finance Ministry's securities department, told Reuters the bonds had been bought by the state savings bank Sberbank, and subsequently purchased by the Central Bank, which now held them on its books.
The paper is not subject to a 15 percent tax on government securities as it had been issued before the tax came into force, Aleksashenko said.
trading in the new paper would be on the same terms as trading in GKO discount Treasury bills and floating-rate OFZ bonds, he said.
Interest on floating-rate OFZ bonds, which are already traded with T-bills on MICEX, is based on the yields of current T-bill issues.

"The only difference of the new paper from the usual OFZs is in the fixed coupon rate," he said. "We are not starting with an auction, but from secondary trading. The Finance Ministry will continue issuing OFZs with fixed rates and placing them at auctions."
Aleksashenko said the issue of the three-year OFZs testified to the government's wish to issue longer-term paper.
The 1997 budget provides for issuing 17-year paper, he said.
